name: LANKO 136 Rapid Patching Mortar
paste:
LANKO® 136 RAPID PATCHING MORTAR: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: LANKO® 136 Rapid Patching Mortar, May 2026, Version 01.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/1/lanko-136-rapid-patchingmortar.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide LANKO® 136 Rapid Patching Mortar where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2026, Version 01.03).
1.2 Product description. LANKO® 136 Rapid Patching Mortar is a 1-part, cementitious, very rapid hardening, early strength gain concrete repair material.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - On, above and below grade on concrete
    - Highway overlays and repairs
    - Structural repair material for concrete roadways, parking structures, bridges, dams and ramps
    - Full depth patching repairs Economical patching material for horizontal repairs of concrete and mortar
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.10.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. LANKO® 136 Rapid Patching Mortar
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Rapid Setting, High Strenght Trafficable Repair Mortar
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (May 2026, Version 01.03) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS 1478.2:2005: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.1).
    - EN 1542: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.1).
    - AS/NZS 2350.4-2006: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Final set time (p.2); Application Information > Initial set time (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Epoxy coatings can be applied as early as 4 hours
    - Freeze / thaw resistant
    - Easy to mix and apply - labor saving
    - High early strength
    - Fast setting
    - Open to foot traffic in 45 minutes
    - Open to vehicle traffic in 1 hour (at 23 °C)
    - Not a vapour barrier
    - Can be placed up to 150mm
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Cement, selected aggregates and special additives
    - Appearance and colour: Grey powder
    - Density: 2,200 kg/m³
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Tensile adhesion strength: ≥ 2.0 MPa (EN 1542)
2.7 Compressive strength.
    | Time | Compressive Strength |
    | 1 hour | ~ 13 MPa |
    | 2 hour | ~ 20 MPa |
    | 1 day | ~ 35 MPa |
    | 7 days | ~ 65 MPa |
    | 28 days | ~ 80 MPa |
    | Material and curing conditions at 23 °C / 50 % r.h., water/powder = 0.11 |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (AS 1478.2:2005)
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 5 kg bag
    - Shelf life: 12 months
    - Storage conditions: Product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between 5 °C and 35 °C. Always refer to packaging.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2026, Version 01.03) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment.
    - Concrete
    - Surface must be clean and sound. Remove all deteriorated concrete, dirt, oil, grease, and other bond-inhibiting materials from the area to be repaired. Be sure repair area is not less than 5 mm deep. Preparation work should be done by appropriate mechanical techniques. Obtain an exposed aggregate surface with a minimum surface profile of 3 mm (CSP 6) on clean, sound concrete. To ensure optimum repair results, the effectiveness of decontamination and preparation should be assessed by a pull-off test. Saw cutting of edges is recommended. Saturate surface to be repaired with clean water. Substrate should be saturated surface dry (SSD) prior to application.
    - Steel reinforcement
    - Rust, scale, mortar, concrete, dust and other loose and deleterious material which reduces bond or contributes to corrosion shall be removed. Surfaces shall be prepared using abrasive blast cleaning techniques or high pressure water-blasting to achieve a bright metal finish.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2026, Version 01.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: 0.530–0.600 L / 5 kg bag
    - Yield: ~ 2.5 litres per 5 kg bag
    - Pot Life: Approximately 15 minutes after adding powder to the water
    - Initial set time: ~ 15 - 20 minutes at 23 °C / 50 % r.h. (AS/NZS 2350.4-2006)
    - Final set time: ~ 25 - 30 minutes at 23 °C / 50 % r.h. (AS/NZS 2350.4-2006)
4.3 Layer thickness.
    | Minimum | Maximum |
    | Mortar | 5 mm | 150 mm |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.4 Mixing.
    - Water mix: Use the minimum amount of water necessary for ease of placement. The recommended water addition is 0.530–0.600 L per 5 kg bag.
    - Mixing sequence: Add 70 % of the required water into the mixing vessel, then gradually add LANKO® 136 Rapid Patching Mortar while mixing. Slowly incorporate the remaining water until the desired consistency is achieved.
    - Site condition adjustments: Mixing ratios may vary based on site conditions. For optimal performance, ensure both the mixing water and substrate are between 5 °C and 30 °C. Small trial batches are recommended to determine the best working consistency.
    - Mixing method: Use an electric drill with a paddle mixer or mix by hand. Mix for approximately 3 minutes to achieve the best results.
4.5 Application. Reinforcement Corrosion Protection / Primer Coating Where a reinforcement coating is required, apply to the whole exposed circumference of the steel the SikaTop-110 EpoCem or Sika Monotop-910N. The repair mortar must be applied into the coating ‘wet’ on ‘dry’.
4.6 Application - Concrete Bonding Primer. Prime the prepared substrate with a scrub coat of LANKO® 136 Rapid Patching Mortar by firmly scraping the scrub coat over the substrate surface to form a thin layer and fill any pores or cavities in the surface. Ensure the whole surface to be repaired is covered by the scrub coat. The repair mortar has to be applied into primer ‘wet’ on ‘wet’.
4.7 Application - Repair Mortar. The prepared mortar must be scrubbed into the substrate. Be sure to fill all pores and voids. force materials against the edge of the repair, working towards the centre. After filling the repair, screed of excess. Allow concrete to set to desired stiffness, then finish. If a smoother finish is desired, a magnesium float should be used. Mixing, placing and finishing should not exceed 15 minutes maximum. To control setting times, cold water should be used in hot weather and hot water used in cold weather.
4.8 Curing treatment. Moist cure should commence immediately after finishing. It is necessary to protect newly applied material from rain. To prevent from freezing, cover with insulating material.
4.9 Cleaning of equipment. LANKO® 136 Rapid Patching Mortar should be removed from tools and equipment immediately after use with clean water. Any cured material may be removed by mechanical means.
4.10 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Apply only to sound, prepared substrate.
    - Avoid application in direct sun and/or strong winds.
    - Do not feather edge.
    - Use only potable water.
    - Variations in aggregates may produce differences in strengths from the typical values stated in Product Data Sheet.
    - For early application of epoxy coatings, on site testing is recommended to verify suitability. Consult the coatings manufacturer for guidance.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. 7 °C minimum
5.3 Substrate temperature. 7 °C minimum
5.4 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Surface must be clean and sound. Remove all deteriorated concrete, dirt, oil, grease, and other bond-inhibiting materials from the area to be repaired. Be sure repair area is not less than 5 mm deep. Preparation work should be done by appropriate mechanical techniques. Obtain an exposed aggregate surface with a minimum surface profile of 3 mm (CSP 6) on clean, sound concrete. To ensure optimum repair results, the effectiveness of decontamination and preparation should be assessed by a pull-off test. Saw cutting of edges is recommended. Saturate surface to be repaired with clean water. Substrate should be saturated surface dry (SSD) prior to application.
    - Site condition adjustments: Mixing ratios may vary based on site conditions. For optimal performance, ensure both the mixing water and substrate are between 5 °C and 30 °C. Small trial batches are recommended to determine the best working consistency.
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: Time | Compressive Strength; 1 hour | ~ 13 MPa; 2 hour | ~ 20 MPa; 1 day | ~ 35 MPa; 7 days | ~ 65 MPa; 28 days | ~ 80 MPa; Material and curing conditions at 23 °C / 50 % r.h., water/powder = 0.11 (AS 1478.2:2005)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: ≥ 2.0 MPa (EN 1542)
    - Initial set time: ~ 15 - 20 minutes at 23 °C / 50 % r.h. (AS/NZS 2350.4-2006)
    - Final set time: ~ 25 - 30 minutes at 23 °C / 50 % r.h. (AS/NZS 2350.4-2006)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: LANKO® 136 Rapid Patching Mortar, May 2026, Version 01.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/1/lanko-136-rapid-patchingmortar.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS LANKO 136 Rapid Patching Mortar, version 18/06/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/l/sds-lanko-136-rapidpatchingmortar.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
